title: He Was Found Dead With No Name. Hidden In His Pocket Was A Two-Word Note.
description:
In 1948, a man was found dead on an Australian beach. No ID, no name, every label cut from his clothes -- and a secret pocket hiding a two-word note that's never been fully explained.

This is one of three real cases in The Vanishing Hours -- true stories, calmly told. The full episode is linked below.

scenes.text: In December of 1948, a man was found dead on a beach in Australia. No wallet. No ID. Every label had been cut out of his clothes.
Nobody could identify him. Not his fingerprints, not his dental records -- nothing, for over seventy years.
Then a pathologist found something the first examination had missed: a tiny hidden pocket, sewn into his trousers.
Inside it was a scrap of paper, torn from a book, with two words printed on it: 'Tamam Shud.' Persian for 'it is finished.'
That wasn't even the strangest part. The book turned up weeks later, with a code written inside that's never been cracked, and a phone number that led straight to a woman who denied ever knowing him.
This is one of three real cases in The Vanishing Hours -- true stories, calmly told, perfect for falling asleep to. The full episode is linked in the description below.
